      Problem: The updated regex patterns `fix(ed|ing)` and `patch(ed|ing)` are missing the suffix-group optional quantifier `?`. The original patterns used `fix(ed|es)?` and `patch(ed|es)?` with the group optional, so they matched base-form "fix"/"patch" as well as "fixed"/"fixes"/"fixing". The new patterns require either "ed" or "ing" immediately after the verb, so base-form verbs no longer match.; The EDITOR_CHANGES_LOST check relies on these patterns to detect edit-like claims inside the editor's Changes section. When the editor uses base-form verbs (e.g., "- fix typo", "- patch vulnerability"), the grep no longer matches, allowing a contradiction between "Change status: not-edited" and actual edit wording to slip through undetected. This is a functional regression that reduces safety coverage.; Additional observations:; - The inline grep at line 2037, the `edit_claim_regex` assignment at line 2064, and the `bullet_edit_regex` assignment at line 2066 all suffer from the same missing `?`.; - The regression is certain: extended regex `(ed|ing)?` makes the group optional; without `?`, only "fix/ patch" followed explicitly by "ed" or "ing" match.; - The PR's intent (avoiding plural-noun false positives like "fixes"/"patches") is still achieved because those forms don't match `(ed|ing)`; restoring the `?` while keeping `es` out of the alternation preserves the fix while also restoring base-form detection: use `fix(ed|ing)?` and `patch(ed|ing)?`.; - The added comment should be updated to reflect the corrected pattern.; - Other verbs in the same patterns (e.g., `improv(e|ed|es|ing)`) have inconsistent optionality across the three locations; the inline grep lacks `?` on the group, so base-form "improve" wouldn't match there either. Those are pre-existing inconsistencies, not introduced by this PR.; No other issues found. The change set is otherwise minimal, consistent across the three modified locations, and correctly scoped to the detection logic.
